entities.summary: Xenophanes of Colophon, a 6th-century Greek philosopher and theologian, left a lasting impact on the development of Western philosophy. Born in ancient Ionia, Xenophanes travelled extensively throughout the Greek-speaking world, critiquing Homer's epic poems and promoting monotheistic worship of the one true god. His ideas influenced prominent figures such as Socrates and Plato, shaping the trajectory of Western thought. Xenophanes' critiques of Homer's mythology also resonated with later ancient Greek thinkers, such as Aristotle. Despite his relatively minor stature compared to other ancient Greek philosophers, Xenophanes' work had a profound effect on the intellectual landscape of the ancient world. His philosophical system, which emphasized the unity of all things and the existence of a single, omniscient deity, foreshadowed later philosophical movements, including Neoplatonism and Christianity. As a poet and critic, Xenophanes' work also continues to be studied by scholars today, offering valuable insights into the intellectual and cultural currents of ancient Greece.
